classification.classification_note: The saved MemorySanitizer report points to `if (leftNeighbor < owner)` in `cellToVertex`, so the witnessed bug is a branch use of an uninitialized stack `H3Index`, not a bounds error.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42515778 (h3): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target fuzzerVertexes [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42515778
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source under `_work/src/h3` / staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced MemorySanitizer's use-of-uninitialized-value at `src/h3lib/lib/vertex.c:229:13` in the staged vulnerable checkout. The exact 16-byte witness makes `fuzzerVertexes` call `cellToVertex()` with `cell = 0x685b2396e900fff9` and `vertexNum = 2`. Under the H3 bit macros this word is treated as a non-pentagon resolution-5 cell with valid base cell 89, but it is malformed because `H3_GET_INDEX_DIGIT(cell, 2) == INVALID_DIGIT` and digits beyond declared resolution 5 are not all `INVALID_DIGIT`. `cellToVertex()` does not validate that structure. It accepts `vertexNum == 2`, enters owner selection, derives a left-neighbor direction, and allocates local `H3Index leftNeighbor;` without initialization. It then calls `h3NeighborRotations(cell, left, &lRotations, &leftNeighbor)` and ignores the returned `H3Error`. The staged fix adds `leftNeighborError` handling and a regression test expecting `E_CELL_INVALID` for this exact `index, vertexNum` pair; because base cell 89 passes `h3NeighborRotations()`'s upfront base-cell check, that nonzero return must come from the helper's later `oldDigit == INVALID_DIGIT` branch, which runs before the success store `*out = current`. Vulnerable execution still falls through to `if (leftNeighbor < owner)`, so the comparison reads the still-uninitialized `leftNeighbor` stack slot and triggers the saved MSan report.

source.description: First project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled `cell` argument and materializes the local shape and resolution state that governs the later validation and neighbor-lookup path.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 16-byte file `f9 ff 00 e9 96 23 5b 68 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 45`. In the reproduced Stage 01 build, the fuzzer's `inputArgs` cast supplies `cell = 0x685b2396e900fff9` and `vertexNum = 2` to `cellToVertex()`, and this statement is the first project-code read of that attacker-controlled `cell`.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. This comparison reads `leftNeighbor` in the branch condition after the failing left-neighbor lookup left that local unwritten.
sink.note: Both `sanitizer_trace.txt` and `reproduction_report.json` identify `src/h3lib/lib/vertex.c:229:13` in `cellToVertex()` as the observed use-of-uninitialized-value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `cellToVertex()` calls `h3NeighborRotations()` on the malformed cell but discards the returned `H3Error`. When the helper rejects the cell before writing `*out`, execution still falls through to line 229 and reads `leftNeighbor` uninitialized.
root_cause.note: The staged fix changes this exact site to `H3Error leftNeighborError = h3NeighborRotations(...); if (leftNeighborError) return leftNeighborError;` and adds a regression test for `0x685b2396e900fff9, vertexNum = 2` expecting `E_CELL_INVALID`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Concrete uninitialized object named by the MSan origin. `leftNeighbor` is a stack local with no initializer, and the neighbor helper only assigns it on success.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: MemorySanitizer says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `leftNeighbor` in the `cellToVertex` stack frame. This declaration is the concrete local slot named by that origin report.
tainted_value_origin.note: If `h3NeighborRotations()` reached its success store `*out = current` at `src/h3lib/lib/algos.c:475`, this slot would become initialized. The later sink proves that write never happened on the witnessed path.

parser_admitted.description: After `size >= sizeof(inputArgs)` and the `inputArgs` cast, the saved witness is passed into `cellToVertex()` as `args->index` and `args->vertexNum`. This is the harness-to-project handoff, not the scored source.

coarse_trace.summary: The malformed H3 cell is interpreted as a non-pentagon resolution-5 cell, `vertexNum == 2` passes the range gate, and `cellToVertex()` enters the owner-determination branch.
A left-neighbor direction is derived for vertex 2, and `cellToVertex()` allocates local `leftNeighbor` to receive the neighbor output.
The left-neighbor helper rejects the malformed cell at its `oldDigit == INVALID_DIGIT` return before its success-only `*out = current` write, but the vulnerable caller ignores that nonzero result.
The comparison `leftNeighbor < owner` reads the still-uninitialized `leftNeighbor` stack slot and triggers the reported MemorySanitizer branch use.

fine_trace.note: Source. `cellToVertex()` first materializes local state from the attacker-controlled `cell`. For the exact witness this path treats `0x685b2396e900fff9` as a non-pentagon cell with `cellNumVerts == 6`, `res == 5`, and base cell 89, even though the same bits are malformed under `isValidCell()` semantics because `H3_GET_INDEX_DIGIT(cell, 2) == INVALID_DIGIT` and the trailing digits beyond resolution 5 are not all `INVALID_DIGIT`.
Control gate. The witness supplies `vertexNum == 2`, so this range check does not reject the call because step 1 set `cellNumVerts == 6` on the non-pentagon path.
Control gate. The witness cell has `res == 5` and resolution digit 5 equal to `3`, not `CENTER_DIGIT`, so `cellToVertex()` enters the owner-determination block and attempts neighbor lookup.

fine_trace.code:
Direction left = directionForVertexNum(cell, vertexNum);
if (left == INVALID_DIGIT) return E_FAILED;
fine_trace.note: Using the admitted `vertexNum == 2`, `cellToVertex()` derives a left-neighbor direction for this vertex. The reproduced crash reaches line 229, so the `left == INVALID_DIGIT` early return at line 224 did not fire for this witness.

Tainted value origin. This out-parameter storage has no initializer before the left-neighbor lookup. `h3NeighborRotations()` writes `*out` only on its success path at `algos.c:475`, so any earlier error return leaves `leftNeighbor` indeterminate. MSan's origin report names allocation of `leftNeighbor` in the `cellToVertex` frame.

Root cause. `cellToVertex()` performs the left-neighbor lookup with the malformed cell and derived `left` direction but never stores or checks the returned `H3Error`. The staged fix changes this exact site to `leftNeighborError = h3NeighborRotations(...); if (leftNeighborError) return leftNeighborError;`, so vulnerable code is missing the only control transfer that would stop the later read of `leftNeighbor` after a helper failure.

During the step-6 left-neighbor traversal, `h3NeighborRotations()` returns `E_CELL_INVALID` before the success store `*out = current`. The witness cell's base cell is 89, so the helper's earlier base-cell check at `algos.c:347-350` cannot be the `E_CELL_INVALID` source; combined with the staged regression for this exact `index, vertexNum` pair, the remaining vulnerable-source explanation is this `oldDigit == INVALID_DIGIT` return path. The out-parameter `leftNeighbor` therefore remains exactly as allocated in step 5.

Sink. After step 7 returns `E_CELL_INVALID` before any `*out` store, vulnerable `cellToVertex()` immediately compares the still-uninitialized `leftNeighbor` against `owner`. This branch is the first observed use that MemorySanitizer reports.

allocation_context.note: MSan says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `leftNeighbor` in the `cellToVertex` stack frame; the concrete local declaration is `H3Index leftNeighbor;` at line 226.

format.name: Exact 16-byte inputArgs witness
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 16-byte file staged at `poc`: `f9 ff 00 e9 96 23 5b 68 02 00 00 00 00 00 00 45`. The harness only continues when `size >= sizeof(inputArgs)`, then reinterprets the bytes as `inputArgs` and calls `cellToVertex(args->index, args->vertexNum, &out)`. In the reproduced Stage 01 build that call used `args->index == 0x685b2396e900fff9` and `args->vertexNum == 2`. Under the H3 source macros this cell is malformed because resolution digit 2 is `INVALID_DIGIT` and digits beyond declared resolution 5 are not all `INVALID_DIGIT`, yet `cellToVertex()` still accepts `vertexNum == 2`, reaches the unchecked `h3NeighborRotations()` call, and then reads uninitialized `leftNeighbor` at line 229. No broader input class is claimed here.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 did not instrument the workspace. The helper's no-write transition is closed statically from the exact witness bit layout, the vulnerable source, the saved MSan origin/sink, and the staged regression added by the fix.
Stage 01 preserved only the vulnerable run. `patch_resolves` is grounded in the staged source diff and regression test, not in an executed fixed-build rerun.
